description: The floating face - a small always-on-top window with only Jarvis's animated face on it, no chat box, no approve/deny, no settings. Its page is floating.html (NOT faces.html itself): it embeds the same faces.html?mode=display&feed=parent frame the Widget's tray already runs, driven by postMessage, so the face - the largest body of third-party-shaped drawing code in the app, and deliberately held to zero event permission everywhere else it appears (capabilities/faces.json) - never holds a Tauri permission of its own. This window's own page needs the read-only state it relays into that frame: jarvis-link (which face state to show) and appearance-read (which face, which colours). It reads jarvis-link.js the same way the widget does, so its own memory - never the face frame's - also carries the full approval queue the module fetches for every surface, an email's whole text included (bug audit 2026-09-27, desktop-rust finding #4); nothing on screen shows any of it, and release builds have no developer tools (Cargo.toml's `devtools` feature) to read that memory from outside this app's own code. Drag-region needs core:window:allow-start-dragging: there is no OS titlebar, so the whole page is what the owner grabs (the face frame sits over it with pointer-events:none, so a click reaches this page, not the iframe). core:event:allow-emit is deliberately NOT here. With "click through" on, Rust has to be told where the face's own picture is drawn before it can decide which clicks to let past the window (`floating-hit-mask`, floating.js's own grid, read by windows.rs's pointer watcher). It is the one thing here this page WRITES rather than reads, and it is a granted command rather than an event on purpose: the rule this app's security suite holds to (apps security audit M1, tests/security.mjs) is that NO window may emit an event, because the quickbar trusts what it hears and a page that could emit could fake the owner's checked voice or an approval card. A granted command carries 1,024 characters of geometry instead: no words, no picture, nothing about the owner, and only while this window is open. No approvals, task-control, widget-surface or focus set: the widget can act on what it shows; this window has no button to act with at all.
